claim: Axis 1 — the registry holds completed+results-posted trials Cochrane missed because they were never published; so registry-k > Cochrane-k for the same question.
verdict: REFUTED for established questions (NEAR-NULL). Reported loudly per pre-registration.

malaria.example_A: NCT00297882 (artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-artesunate, cure rate D28, 2009) — genuine ACT efficacy trial, results posted, never published

cross_vendor: agy/Gemini classified the 11 malaria candidates 1 A / 3 B / 7 C — agrees the standard-matchable count is 1.
honest_interpretation: The registry-only pool is real and large (47/54), but ~78% are mechanistic (safety/PK/immunogenicity) and the efficacy ones are overwhelmingly NOVEL-drug Phase-II (no existing review) or challenge models. For an ESTABLISHED clinical-efficacy question, the registry adds ~1 trial a journal-based review missed — a near-null. Naive PICO counting over-states 'Cochrane missed N' by ~20-50x (matcher FP ~98%, matching the orphan-trial failure mode). The narrow-and-deep advantage is NOT on raw trial-count-per-established-question; it is real on harms (gap 55-88%), outcome switching (6%), and pre-registered targets. The surviving Axis-1 value is narrower and honest: the registry surfaces unpublished EFFICACY results for EMERGING drugs (SJ733, artefenomel, cipargamin) before/without journal publication.
named_blocker: Exact per-review non-overlap needs the pairwise70 gold set (machine-readable PICO + included-trial NCTs, owned by local_beae89ce) and CDSR access — neither in this tree. And modern Cochrane searches trial registries, so 'non-published' does not guarantee 'review missed it' — further shrinking the count.
